target_customer: Utility-scale solar developers, EPC contractors and owners buying single-axis trackers
problem: Conventional motorized trackers have many moving parts and high installed cost and maintenance, which raises the cost of solar energy.
business_model: Hardware sales of balance-of-system products, mainly the T29 pneumatic single-axis tracker, per project

founders.name: Leila Madrone
founders.background_notes: Canary Media gives her prior employers. Latitude Media calls her founder and former CTO. The company was a spin out of Otherlab per trade press.

exit.reason: Existing investors could not commit more capital; the company cited a steel cost gap between the US and Asia and a polymer supply disruption

competitors.name: Nextracker
competitors.traction_then: About a third of global tracker shipments in 2017 out of 14.5 GW

competitors.name: Array Technologies
competitors.traction_then: Second in global shipments in 2017 with about 14 percent

technical_complexity.rationale: Used air-filled polymer bladders in place of motors and gears, requiring novel materials, controls and reliability across years of field use. Patents cover the pneumatic drive.

defensibility.rationale: Patented AirDrive technology differed from steel and motor trackers, but incumbents with large share and bankability could adapt and buyers wanted bankable track records.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports an incumbent copying or buying Sunfolding. The company closed in 2023 after its investors would not fund more.

market_need_then: Global tracker shipments grew 32 percent in 2017 to 14.5 GW and the market was led by two firms, so demand for lower-cost trackers was growing.

branding.domain_note: sunfolding.com now redirects to hexxen.com, an unrelated site, so the original domain is gone.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and project-focused in press releases

branding.brand_signature: AirDrive pneumatic tracker with air bladders instead of motors

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the product and funding, but no evidence of brand pull beyond the solar industry. No name origin or logo source was found.

outcome_analysis: Sunfolding raised a Series A in 2017, a 32 million dollar Series B in 2019 and, per one database, a Series C in late 2022, but wound down in 2023. The founder said existing investors were tapped out. A pause around 2020, a US versus Asian steel cost gap and a polymer supply disruption after an earthquake hurt it, and a former employee pointed to manufacturing difficulty and limited project experience. It never reached the scale of Nextracker or Array.
notes: Series C of 21.4M on 2022-12-27 rests on a single database (CB Insights snippet) and no second outlet confirmed it; the amount could include other financing. Series A in 2017 is stated by Latitude Media with no amount or investors found. Canary Media lists Citylight Capital, Alumni Ventures and Elemental Excelerator as other backers, not tied to a specific round. Competitor sources are dated February 2018, about six months after the Summer 2017 batch, and describe 2017 shipments. The company website redirects to an unrelated domain. The 2019 press release names CEO Jurgen Krehnke and Canary names CEO Glen Davis in 2023; neither is recorded as a founder. The shutdown date is only given as 2023 (a CEO departure in October 2023 appears on LinkedIn per Canary). Name origin and logo not found.
